facts.claim: go/go.mod, go/Dockerfile and .github/workflows/ci.yml are the only paths that changed since v1.9.2. go/go.mod changes only its go line, from 1.26.9 to 1.27.2; its requirements and go/go.sum are unchanged. The image's builder moves from golang:1.26.9-alpine to golang:1.27.2-alpine, pinned by the index digest sha256:85dc1069ac644ea3c527b177303a406eb3358192816cd7f9e5848eb658851673. In ci.yml only the staticcheck step changed: staticcheck 2026.2.1 (v0.8.1) as published stops on this source built by Go 1.27.2 with 'export data version 5 is greater than maximum supported version 4' (dominikh/go-tools#1832), so the step builds that release against golang.org/x/tools v0.51.0 and runs the result; go/staticcheck.conf still selects the checks. govulncheck stays at v1.5.0 and, run by Go 1.27.2, finds no vulnerabilities.

evidence.source: git diff v1.9.2..HEAD; go/go.mod; go/Dockerfile; .github/workflows/ci.yml; docker buildx imagetools inspect golang:1.27.2-alpine; staticcheck v0.8.1 and govulncheck v1.5.0 run by Go 1.27.2

facts.claim: Go 1.27 binaries need macOS 13 Ventura or later. With the module's go line at 1.27, two GODEBUG defaults change for this program: x509sslcertoverrideplatform=1, so on Windows and macOS crypto/x509 loads roots from SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR when either is set instead of using the platform verifier, and tracebacklabels=1, which adds runtime/pprof goroutine labels to tracebacks; the source sets no goroutine labels. Go 1.27 removes the GODEBUG settings gotypesalias, tlsunsafeekm, tlsrsakex, tls3des, tls10server, x509keypairleaf and asynctimerchan; no file in this repository names any of them, and the source has no //go:debug directive or godebug line. The toolchain also backs encoding/json with its v2 implementation, which keeps marshalling and unmarshalling behaviour but may word errors differently, limits a net/http server to 500 header values per request unless Server.MaxHeaderValueCount is set, and drains unread content, up to a limit, when an HTTP/1 response body is closed.

The confirmed review release-v1.9.2 covers v1.9.1..ab32648eb548 and, with the confirmed reviews release-v1.9.0 and release-v1.9.1 it cites, describes every change since v1.8.0; v1.9.2 adds only that review's own files after ab32648eb548.

No Go source file, test, console file, document or script changed since v1.9.2, and the only workflow change is the staticcheck step: the binary is built from the source v1.9.2 builds, by Go 1.27.2 instead of Go 1.26.9, and it embeds v1.9.2's console bundle.

Exploratory run run-20261009T015304-75rbpy of draft llm-gateway, the draft that became contract da05219969e0, against a binary built by Go 1.27.2 from 728a96ce38c7 and served with LLMGW_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_API=1 as the release smoke serves it, passed all ten assertions, and its chain verifies.

For source revision 728a96ce38c7bce03f0a42591b9b63e2f987143b built by Go 1.27.2: go build, go vet, gofmt, go mod tidy -diff, go mod verify, staticcheck built as ci.yml builds it, and govulncheck v1.5.0 pass; go test passes for every package on windows/amd64 and linux/amd64, and go test -race for every package on linux/amd64; all eight release targets cross-compile; and the deterministic Docker acceptance passes all 31 checks against an image built from it with the new builder on a Linux engine, where its digest policy does not apply to a locally built candidate. actionlint passes on the changed workflow, and the documentation check passes.

evidence.source: local and remote Linux test execution

conclusion.summary: The release ships v1.9.2's source built by Go 1.27.2 instead of Go 1.26.9: only the module's go line, the image's builder and CI's staticcheck step changed. Go 1.27 needs macOS 13 or later and, at the module's new go version, honours SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR on Windows and macOS; neither bears on an accepted proposition. Every accepted proposition holds for this source, and the exploratory run, the unit tests, the race run and the Docker acceptance exercise them.
